*How much to write: about 9 lines · 5 minutes.*

$\sqrt{2\sin2x}=\sqrt{4\sin x\cos x}=2\cos x\sqrt{\tan x}$, so the integrand is $\dfrac{1}{2\cos^4x\sqrt{\tan x}}=\dfrac{\sec^4x}{2\sqrt{\tan x}}$

Put $t=\tan x$, $dt=\sec^2x\,dx$, and $\sec^2x=1+t^2$. Limits: $x=0\to t=0$; $x=\dfrac\pi4\to t=1$.

<mark>$I=\dfrac12\displaystyle\int_0^1\dfrac{1+t^2}{\sqrt t}\,dt$</mark> $=\dfrac12\displaystyle\int_0^1\left(t^{-1/2}+t^{3/2}\right)dt=\dfrac12\left[2\sqrt t+\dfrac25t^{5/2}\right]_0^1=\dfrac12\left(2+\dfrac25\right)$

$$\boxed{\dfrac65}$$

:::tip Your answer must contain
- $\sin2x=2\sin x\cos x$
- limits changed to $t$
- the powers of $t$ integrated term by term
:::

**Marks are lost for:** keeping the limits $0$ and $\dfrac\pi4$ after substituting.
hint: Pull $\cos x$ out of the root to make $\sqrt{\tan x}$; then $t=\tan x$.

*How much to write: about 9 lines · 5 minutes.*

Integrate by parts with $\tan^{-1}x$ as the first function (ILATE):

$I=\left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}\tan^{-1}x\right]_0^1-\dfrac12\displaystyle\int_0^1\dfrac{x^2}{1+x^2}\,dx$

Write <mark>$\dfrac{x^2}{1+x^2}=1-\dfrac{1}{1+x^2}$</mark>: $\ I=\dfrac\pi8-\dfrac12\Big[x-\tan^{-1}x\Big]_0^1$

$=\dfrac\pi8-\dfrac12\left(1-\dfrac\pi4\right)=\dfrac\pi8-\dfrac12+\dfrac\pi8$

$$\boxed{\dfrac\pi4-\dfrac12}$$

:::tip Your answer must contain
- $\tan^{-1}x$ chosen as the first function
- the split of $\dfrac{x^2}{1+x^2}$
- limits applied to every term
:::

label: PYQ (2026)
model_answer:
*How much to write: about 9 lines · 5 minutes.*

Multiply numerator and denominator inside the root by $x+2$: $I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x+2}{\sqrt{x^2-4}}\,dx$

Split: $I=\displaystyle\int\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{x^2-4}}\,dx+2\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2-4}}$

First part: put $t=x^2-4$, giving <mark>$\sqrt{x^2-4}$</mark>. Second part is the standard form $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2-a^2}}$ with $a=2$.

$$\boxed{\sqrt{x^2-4}+2\log\left|x+\sqrt{x^2-4}\right|+C}$$

:::tip Your answer must contain
- the rationalising step
- the two integrals shown separately
- $+C$
:::

**Marks are lost for:** dropping the factor 2 on the log term; leaving out the modulus or $+C$.
hint: Multiply inside the root by $\dfrac{x+2}{x+2}$.

label: PYQ (2026)
model_answer:
*How much to write: about 9 lines · 5 minutes.*

Put $x^2=t$ (for the partial fractions only): $\dfrac{t}{(t+9)(t+16)}=\dfrac{A}{t+9}+\dfrac{B}{t+16}$

$t=A(t+16)+B(t+9)$. At $t=-9$: $A=-\dfrac97$. At $t=-16$: $B=\dfrac{16}{7}$.

$I=-\dfrac97\displaystyle\int\dfrac{dx}{x^2+9}+\dfrac{16}{7}\int\dfrac{dx}{x^2+16}$ <mark>$=-\dfrac97\cdot\dfrac13\tan^{-1}\dfrac x3+\dfrac{16}{7}\cdot\dfrac14\tan^{-1}\dfrac x4+C$</mark>

$$\boxed{\dfrac47\tan^{-1}\dfrac x4-\dfrac37\tan^{-1}\dfrac x3+C}$$

:::tip Your answer must contain
- the note that $x^2=t$ is not a substitution in the integral
- $\dfrac1a\tan^{-1}\dfrac xa$ with the $\dfrac1a$
:::

**Marks are lost for:** writing $dt$ in place of $dx$; forgetting $\dfrac13$ and $\dfrac14$.
hint: Treat $x^2$ as a single letter to split the fraction, then integrate in $x$.

$1+\cos2x=2\cos^2x$, so $I_1=\dfrac12\displaystyle\int_{-\pi/4}^{\pi/4}\sec^2x\,dx=\dfrac12\Big[\tan x\Big]_{-\pi/4}^{\pi/4}=\dfrac12(1+1)=1$

$\lvert x\rvert$ is an <u>even</u> function: $I_2=2\displaystyle\int_0^{1/2}x\,dx=2\left[\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^{1/2}=\dfrac14$

<mark>$I_1-4I_2=1-4\times\dfrac14=0$</mark>

:::tip Your answer must contain
- $1+\cos2x=2\cos^2x$
- the even-function property (or the modulus split at 0)
- the final line
:::
